ELG: Gross Motor Skills 
 
Children at the expected level of development will: 
✓ Negotiate space and obstacles safely, with consideration for themselves and others; 
✓ Demonstrate strength, balance and coordination when playing; 
✓ Move energetically, such as running, jumping, dancing, hopping, skipping and climbing. 
 
ELG: Fine Motor Skills 
 
Children at the expected level of development will: 
✓ Hold a pencil effectively in preparation for fluent writing – using the tripod grip in almost all cases; 
✓ Use a range of small tools, including scissors, paint brushes and cutlery; 
✓ Begin to show accuracy and care when drawing 
What are we thinking? 
 obstacles – these could be furniture/resources in the learning environment, around the school, resources used in PE, in the playground, 
initiated by themselves in their play and even other children near by. 
 Demonstrate strength, balance and coordination – you will know if the child has grasped these skills with confidence by their success 
and how much risk they take in their play – e.g. moving on one leg, climbing, standing tll on obstacles off the ground.  
 Such as – so this means they do not necessarily have to achieve all of the skills in the following list, they are merely examples of when 
children can move energetically! 
 
 effectively – the outcome on the page will indicate whether the child’s hold is at the stage desired to think about fluent writing. 
 Using a tripod grip – there will be some children that can write fluently, with accuracy and care who do not user the tripod grip – so they 
would be those cases indictated in the ELG that you can use your professional judgement and best fit decision for. 
 Use a range – this does not state that they necessarily need to be used effectibely, but in lone with the rest of this ELG, we think that 
the child should at least be beginning to use them for the desired purpose to be achieved. 
 .including – doesn’t necessarily mean all of these, there may be many more as well to add to the list of small tolls – think of your ‘best fit’ 
option too. 
 Begin to – although this might sound like an ‘emerging’ statement, it indicates that they have the acquired skills of using a pencil but are 
beginning to use this with accuracy, so this is more the next level for this skill. 
 accuracy and care – if the child is using tools effectively then they will be able to show real images in their drawing 
 
See aspects of PD above in bold italics. These are hugely important and are not in the goals. Ensure these are considered when the 
goals are and are noted for a child if they have not achieved this part.
